checks.finding: REQ-001..REQ-007 each specify measurable, downstream-decidable criteria: exact required-field lists, regex patterns (id/name/context), exit-code semantics, stderr line-per-violation format, and byte-level non-regression for v1 (REQ-007). Every in-scope requirement gives an implementer/verifier a concrete pass/fail test.

acceptance-tests.md Positive-capability matrix row for G1 states the capability as 'concept の全 required フィールドと optional フィールドが表現できる' (all required AND optional fields are representable), citing AC-003 and AC-004. But that same row's own 'proves' column self-limits to 'must_not_own / distinguished_from / responsibilities を持つ契約が受理される（AC-003 が Fulfillment.must_not_own と相互 distinguished_from、AC-004 が Book.must_not_own を含む）' — it never mentions stakeholder_perspectives, an optional field declared in requirements.md's Field Definitions table (`concepts[].stakeholder_perspectives[] | {actor, concern}[]、両者 required・minLength 1 | No`). Scanning the entire AC table confirms no positive AC anywhere (AC-003, AC-004, AC-005, AC-025) populates stakeholder_perspectives with valid data; every mention of the field (AC-020 key-missing, AC-023 minLength, AC-024 type-mismatch) is negative-path only. So the row's claimed capability ('all optional fields representable') is broader than its own evidence, and no other row substitutes. A task author implementing TEST-003/TEST-004 has no AC obligating a positive stakeholder_perspectives fixture, so a schema/validator defect that incorrectly rejects a valid populated stakeholder_perspectives array would go undetected (a stuck-shut risk the spec is otherwise careful to canary for elsewhere, e.g. AC-018's pattern-boundary positives, AC-020's 'optional absent still passes' note). This is a Phase 1 acceptance-criteria completeness gap in the matrix itself, not something a later quality gate could catch after task authors have already built tests around the under-specified claim. Per calibration, 'missing observable acceptance criterion' is Major.

All 25 ACs specify externally observable outcomes: exit code (0 or non-0), stderr content (field name, 1-line-per-violation), or structural assertion result. Negative ACs additionally specify which error text must distinguish adjacent failure modes (e.g. AC-014 key-missing vs AC-018 pattern vs AC-023 minLength), which is concretely checkable by a verifier.

Non-goals section explicitly excludes: concept-test skill/bootstrap (Phase 1), concept-model.template/interviewer changes (Phase 2), reviewer A/B check additions (Phase 3), reverse mode/C4 (Phase 4), v1->v2 migration tooling/dual-version loader (permanently out per owner decision, INV-009), domain/ Markdown artifact generation, and mechanical enforcement of meta.status Approved. The boundary between Phase 0 (this feature) and later phases is explicit and unambiguous.

Material constraints are stated explicitly: additive-only change with byte-level non-regression for v1 (REQ-007), content-as-data / no network / no external dependency constraints (Security Boundaries), and the approval-boundary question is directly addressed rather than left implicit — Roles and Permissions states 'meta.status の Approved 書込に対する機械的強制は存在しない...承認境界は人間のレビュー運用のみが担保する' and cross-references INV-008 for why hook-guard does not protect these artifacts.

R1 (concepts[] type insufficiency), R2 (hand-rolled validator vs schema drift), and R3 (sh/ps1 twin verdict mismatch) each name a concrete mitigation tied to a planned validation surface — R1 to the fixture corpus (REQ-005) preemptively covering Phase 1's 4 judgment types, R2 to REQ-006's drift-lock test, R3 to REQ-006's twin-parity test (also AC-013). All three high-risk claims have a connected validation surface.

Skipped per check's explicit skip condition. investigation.md INV-009 records that sdd-forge itself has no `domain/` directory ('sdd-forge 自身に domain/ ディレクトリは存在せず（ルート直下確認）'), so there is no `domain/context-map.md` with Domain-Model-Status: Approved and no domain-contract.json to check Bounded-Context/terms conformance against.
